findings.finding: The two plan-review-integrated regression tests — `test_a_malformed_local_status_event_does_not_block_a_legitimate_foreign_gap_fill` and `test_a_local_decision_in_the_outbox_only_still_blocks_a_foreign_override` — appear nowhere in the mini-plan's file list or work breakdown. findings.suggestion: Add both tests to the step-1 RED list and the Test Completeness Ledger reference.  3. Category: risk — Severity: low

findings.finding: Deliberate asymmetry: the advisory `pendingDelivery` marker (via `cross_tree_delivery_facts`) will still report a foreign status as "pending" even when it can no longer affect resolution. This is a defensible design choice and well-argued in the rejected alternative, but combined with the disclosed stale `format_pending_delivery_notice` wording, users may act on a "pending" notice that structurally cannot flip the card. Filing a follow-up card is acceptable, but the two staleness items (wording + marker semantics) should be one tracked follow-up, not scattered.
findings.suggestion: Consolidate finding 3 of the plan review and the WebUI parity item into the single follow-up card step 6 already plans, or confirm they're both in it.  4. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: Multiple foreign `status` events for the same gap-fill id: the spec and plan only discuss a single foreign event. Behavior should be unchanged (chronological among foreign events for undecided ids), but it's worth one assertion so a future refactor of the drop-filter doesn't accidentally drop all but one foreign status.
findings.suggestion: One-line assertion in the new gap-fill test: two foreign status events for the same never-decided id resolve to the later one.  5. Category: approach — Severity: low (positive)

findings.finding: The rejected alternative (filtering at the source in `triage_cross_tree`) is correctly rejected — it would invert the module dependency and leak resolution policy into a report-only module. Filtering in `read_all_items` pass 2 is the right boundary, and the plan review's confirmation that local files are read once (not twice) removes the main perf concern.  Security: No new serialized formats, no user-facing surface, no injection surface — the change is in-process resolution logic. No concerns.  Overall: The approach is sound and the module-boundary reasoning is solid; the plan just hasn't fully absorbed its own plan-review findings — the STATUSES filter and the two integrated tests must appear in the mini-plan itself before build. Splitting and recombining raw lines can accidentally change the existing `(ts, file-order)` tie behavior for `amend` records. The rewritten status tie test no longer protects that behavior, and the proposed amend test is not explicitly an equal-timestamp, cross-origin ordering test.
findings.suggestion: Add a regression with local and foreign `amend` events at the same timestamp and assert the current source/file ordering remains unchanged (including the expected foreign-after-local ordering if that is today’s contract).

findings.finding: The separate WebUI resolver is explicitly known to implement the same precedence logic but will remain unfixed. If users can view the same board through both readers before the follow-up ships, the application will present contradictory card states for locally decided items.
findings.suggestion: Before releasing, confirm whether the WebUI is an active status-resolving consumer. If so, coordinate the follow-up release or clearly gate/communicate the temporary inconsistency; otherwise document why the Python reader is the sole affected production path.

findings.finding: The correctness of the local-status gate depends on preserving pass-2 validation semantics: only records that are valid status transitions should establish local authority. The internal review identifies this, but the implementation step itself only says “local `status` event,” which is easy to implement too broadly.
findings.suggestion: Make the invariant explicit in the implementation notes and tests: include an id in `local_status_ids` only when its `newStatus` is in `STATUSES`, using the same normalization/validation path as pass 2. Keep the malformed-local/valid-foreign gap-fill regression as a required test.  Overall, the precedence rule belongs in `read_all_items` and the chosen boundary is sound. Subject to preserving amendment tie ordering and confirming the known multi-reader rollout implication, this is a focused, low-risk fix.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

doubt.disposition: diff touches no migrations, no async/concurrency, no cross-plugin imports, no irreversible ops — in-process JSONL resolution-logic change only; Stage-3 doubt-reviewer trigger criteria (shipwright-build:doubt-reviewer) do not apply

findings.file: shared/scripts/triage.py — the drop-filter inside `read_all_items`'s pass-2 comprehension (`and raw.get("id") in local_status_ids`)
findings.finding: The `id` of a foreign record is used in a set-membership test with no type guard, unlike the local side which is guarded by `isinstance(r.get("id"), str)`. A foreign (sibling-worktree) record whose `id` is a non-string JSON value that is unhashable (e.g. a list or object: `{"event":"status","id":["x"],"newStatus":"dismissed",...}`) raises `TypeError: unhashable type` during the `in local_status_ids` check, crashing `read_all_items` entirely. Before this change, pass 2 only did dict-key lookups on `raw.get("id")` (hash-safe with `.get`-style access on `resolved`), so a single corrupted line in any of the 91 sibling logs — exactly the environment the module's own tolerant-parsing contract exists for — now takes down the whole board read, not just that record.
findings.suggestion: Guard the foreign side symmetrically, e.g. `and isinstance(raw.get("id"), str) and raw.get("id") in local_status_ids`, or hoist the check into a helper that returns False for non-str/non-hashable ids. Add a regression test with a malformed foreign id.

findings.finding: The test asserts the gap-fill resolves `dismissed`, which is also the outcome a correct pre-fix implementation produced (the malformed local status was always skipped, foreign chronology applied). It does distinguish filter-present vs. filter-absent for the gate (without the `newStatus in STATUSES` filter the foreign event would be dropped and status would stay `triage`), so it does validate the specific finding it targets — but only via the `statusBy == "cli"` assertion path. If pass 2 ever tolerated the malformed `newStatus` differently, the assertion could pass for the wrong reason. Minor; the primary assertion (`status == "dismissed"` plus `statusBy`) is adequate but a `status != "triage"`-style negative control alongside an invalid foreign counterpart (asserting it's skipped) would harden it.
findings.suggestion: Optionally add the mirror case: a malformed foreign status must be ignored, not crash (ties into the finding above).
